mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous collapse of WORKPLACES and TRANSIT in the final week reflects the imposition of a state-of-alarm lockdown. This policy shock removes the commuting and transit-linked foot traffic that feeds retail and recreation visits, so RETAIL_REC will remain depressed or fall further over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both drop more than 10 points week-on-week from prior positive levels into negative territory
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from 9.9 to -1.7 and TRANSIT fell from 11.4 to -2.0 in the last observed week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the last 28-day mean despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remaining suppressed, indicating the policy shock did not transmit to retail mobility.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp spike in GROCERY_PHARM to 18.4 reflects panic-buying ahead of anticipated restrictions. This is a transient behavioral surge that pulls forward consumption; once stockpiling is complete, households reduce all discretionary outings including retail and recreation trips, lowering RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises more than 15 points above its 3-week prior baseline in a single week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from 11.0 to 18.4 while RETAIL_REC fell from 2.1 to 0.1 in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rebounds or stabilizes within two weeks even though GROCERY_PHARM remains elevated, showing no substitution effect from grocery stockpiling to reduced retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC's own recent trajectory (1.3, 2.4, 2.1, 0.1) shows deceleration and a sharp drop in the latest week. This momentum pattern, absent any intervention, is expected to persist into the immediate next week, producing a continued decline in RETAIL_REC relative to its recent average.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell from 2.1 to 0.1 in the most recent week after two weeks of growth
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC reverses and rises back above 2.0 within one week, contradicting a simple momentum-continuation pattern.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT jointly collapsing removes the combined commute-and-errand mobility chain that typically links getting to work with incidental retail stops. The interaction of simultaneous declines in both series amplifies the drop in RETAIL_REC beyond what either series alone would predict, driving a sustained four-week decline.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT turned negative simultaneously in the last observed week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decline over the next 28 days is no larger than the decline attributable to either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT alone, indicating no amplifying interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: The rise in PARKS to 8.1 in mid-March could reflect a seasonal uptick in outdoor activity as weather warms, which historically correlates with increased recreation-related retail visits (e.g., cafes, outdoor shopping). If this seasonal effect dominates, RETAIL_REC should see a modest increase over the next two weeks as warmer weather draws people outside.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from 0.6 to 8.1 in the final observed week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to fall even as PARKS remains elevated, showing the seasonal outdoor-activity signal was overridden by other factors such as policy restrictions.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility crossing from negative into positive territory (from -1.7 to 2.0) indicates a behavioral shift toward staying home. Once RESIDENTIAL crosses zero and keeps rising, households systematically substitute outside errands for home-based activity, which should suppress RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL crosses from negative to positive week-on-week (increase greater than 2 points)
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL moved from -1.7 to 2.0 in the latest week, its first positive reading in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining positive and increasing, showing the home-substitution mechanism does not hold.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, TRANSIT mobility acts as a leading indicator because transit suspensions and travel bans are typically imposed before or alongside retail closures. A sharp week-on-week fall in TRANSIT during this regime should precede and predict a parallel fall in RETAIL_REC within two weeks as closures propagate.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 10 points week-on-week while regime is tightening restrictions
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from 11.4 to -2.0 in the last observed week, coincident with the policy shock
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to decline within two weeks of the TRANSIT drop, or declines before TRANSIT does, indicating TRANSIT is not a leading indicator in this regime.

mechanism_narrative: Under lockdown, essential categories like GROCERY_PHARM remain exempted and elevated while non-essential categories like RETAIL_REC are legally restricted or closed. This growing divergence between GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC reflects an essential-vs-non-essential policy split that will persist and widen, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose to 18.4 while RETAIL_REC fell to 0.1 in the same week, a growing gap
failure_condition: The gap between GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC narrows or reverses over the next four weeks, with RETAIL_REC recovering despite continued lockdown, contradicting the essential/non-essential divergence mechanism.
